messages:
olivia (runtime): heads up — noticed p99 jump on prod after we flipped the int8-kernel default this morning. p50 stable, but p99 doubled for short seq requests.

sam (scheduling): curious — did batch size distribution change? could be microbatching interactions with max_wait_ms / max_batch_tokens.

olivia (runtime): yes distribution shifted: more tiny requests stayed alone or 2-3 tokens, but our max_batch_tokens was still high so scheduler waited longer to pack. I grabbed a flamegraph from the runtime:

jing (mlperf): can you paste the flame snippet? also KV hitrate? small seqs hurt kv reuse.

olivia (runtime): pasted snippet below from 1h window (prod-rt-1):
```
flame: serve_loop -> schedule_batch -> wait_for_batch (35%) -> kernel_dispatch (50%) -> kv_lookup (5%) -> kernel_exec_int8 (10%)
note: wait_for_batch jumped to 35% (was ~10% pre-swap)
```

olivia (runtime): KV hitrate dropped ~6% on short prompts, looks like cache keys include quantized shapes and we created a new kernel path that uses different key attrs.

kai (infra): that explains cold KV misses. Maybe kernel switch introduced a different model signature key. Can you grep KV keys? `kubectl exec -c runtime prod-rt-1 -- cat /var/log/kv-keys.log | tail -n 50`

olivia (runtime): ran that — saw `model:openx-int8 v2 | seq_len_bucket:8` vs `model:openx-qt v1 | seq_len_bucket:8` before. so keys diverge on kernel_tag.

sam (scheduling): from the scheduling side, having a large `max_batch_tokens` + `max_wait_ms` = 50ms means microbursts of tiny requests get delayed trying to fill big token budget. For tail SLO we usually bias toward smaller max_batch_tokens for short-seq workloads.

jing (mlperf): propose experiment matrix: (A) reduce max_wait_ms 50->10, (B) reduce max_batch_tokens 4096->1024, (C) add kernel-key-normalization so KV ignores kernel_tag for cache lookup. Run combos and measure p95/p99 + throughput.

olivia (runtime): already ran quick A+B on canary: p99 fell ~30%, p50 same, throughput down ~3% during peak. KV hit recovered half of the lost delta. Full logs: `perf-bot` reported:
```
perf-bot: canary-2248 - p50: 23ms -> 22ms, p95: 68ms -> 65ms, p99: 310ms -> 210ms, qps: 1280 -> 1245
```

kai (infra): 3% qps loss is acceptable if tail improves. But we need to ensure no regression for long-seq batches where bigger batch tokens win. Can we make scheduler aware of seq_len distribution per route?

sam (scheduling): yes — add `route_policy: short_seq_favor_fast` that sets `max_batch_tokens` lower and `max_wait_ms` lower for requests with estimated seq_len < 64. We already compute estimated tokens from metadata.

jing (mlperf): also reconcile kernel-key: we should decouple cache key from kernel variant unless kernel changes output semantics. Add normalization and a compatibility check to map int8 kernel keys to baseline keys.

olivia (runtime): action list: 1) roll kernel-key-normalization to canary (olivia) 2) add route_policy short_seq_favor_fast and test A/B on canary traffic (sam) 3) run full sweep of (A,B,C) combos for 24h and capture p50/p95/p99 + kv_hitrate (jing) 4) telemetry check for long-seq routes to avoid throughput cliffs (kai).

sam (scheduling): I'll enqueue PR for policy and add metrics: `scheduler.wait_ms_distribution`, `batch_tokens_histogram`, `route_seq_len_pct`.

olivia (runtime): logging of decisions will include `reason=waited_for_tokens` or `reason=timeout` in the batch proto to help triage. I'll attach sample traces once PRs land. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout at 2024-09-15T14:20Z for 5% traffic — change: kernel-key-normalization + route_policy.

perf-bot: perf experiment created -> /experiments/224888_canary_microbatch_matrix (runs 24h, metrics captured every 5m).

jing (mlperf): thanks — if canary looks good, we can make kernel default but keep route_policy enabled as safety. Also add an alert if p99 > 2x baseline for >10min.

olivia (runtime): noted. I'll post results to this thread after the 24h run. :eyes:
